questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let \([\,\cdot\,]\) denote the greatest integer function. If the domain of the function \(f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4x+2[x]}{3}\right)\) is \([\alpha,\beta]\), then \(12(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.solution: For arccos, -3<=4x+2[x]<=3. Splitting by floor intervals gives x in [-1/4,0) when [x]=-1 and x in [0,3/4] when [x]=0; all other integer intervals give no solutions. Thus [alpha,beta]=[-1/4,3/4] and 12(alpha+beta)=6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If the set of all solutions of \(|x^2+x-9|=|x|+|x^2-9|\) is \([\alpha,\beta]\cup[\gamma,\infty)\), then \((\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)\) is equal to:
questions.solution: Since x^2+x-9=x+(x^2-9), |A+B|=|A|+|B| iff AB>=0 gives x(x-3)(x+3)>=0. Hence x in [-3,0] union [3,infinity), so alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2=9+0+9=18.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let \(z\) be a complex number such that \(|z+2|=|z-2|\) and \(\arg\left(\frac{z+3}{z-i}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\). Then \(|z|^2\) is equal to:
questions.solution: |z+2|=|z-2| implies Re(z)=0, so z=iy. Then (z+3)/(z-i)=(y-3i)/(y-1). Argument pi/4 requires equal positive real and imaginary parts, so y=-3; both parts are 3/4. Thus |z|^2=|-3i|^2=9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The number of functions f:{1,2,3,4}→{a,b,c}, which are not onto, is:
questions.solution: Total functions=3^4=81. By inclusion-exclusion, onto functions=3^4-3(2^4)+3(1^4)=36. Therefore not-onto functions=81-36=45.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let S={A=[a b; c d]: a,b,c,d∈{0,1,2,3,4} and A²−4A+3I=0} be a set of 2×2 matrices. Then the number of matrices in S, for which the sum of the diagonal elements is equal to 4, is:
questions.solution: A^2-4A+3I=0 gives eigenvalues 1,3; trace 4 forces one of each, so det(A)=3. With a+d=4 and ad-bc=3, diagonal pairs (0,4),(1,3),(2,2),(3,1),(4,0) require bc=-3,0,1,0,-3, yielding 0,9,1,9,0 ordered (b,c) pairs. Total=19.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&2\\-2&0&1\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}\). Then the sum of all elements of the matrix \(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}(2(\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}))\) is equal to:
questions.solution: det(A)=-4 and X=2(adj A)^(-1)=2A/det(A)=-A/2. For 3x3 X, adj(adj X)=det(X)X; det(X)=(-1/2)^3(-4)=1/2. The result is -A/4. Since the sum of entries of A is 12, the requested sum is -3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The first term of an A.P. of 30 non-negative terms is 10/3. If the sum of this A.P. is the cube of its last term, then its common difference is:
questions.solution: Let last term l. S30=15(10/3+l)=50+15l=l^3, so l^3-15l-50=(l-5)(l^2+5l+10)=0. The quadratic has negative discriminant, hence l=5. Then 5=10/3+29d, giving d=5/87.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The number of ways of forming a queue of 4 boys and 3 girls such that all the girls are not together, is:
questions.solution: All queues: 7!=5040. With all girls together, treat them as a block: 5! ways for the 5 entities and 3! within the block, total 720. Hence 5040-720=4320.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let the smallest value of \(k\in\mathbb N\), for which the coefficient of \(x^3\) in \((1+x)^3+(1+x)^4+(1+x)^5+\cdots+(1+x)^{99}+(1+kx)^{100}\), \(x\ne0\), is \(\left(43n+\frac{101}{4}\right)\binom{100}{3}\) for some \(n\in\mathbb N\), be \(p\). Then the value of \(p+n\) is:
questions.solution: The x^3 coefficient in sum_{r=3}^{99}(1+x)^r is sum C(r,3)=C(100,4); the last term contributes C(100,3)k^3. Using C(100,4)/C(100,3)=97/4 gives k^3-1=43n. For positive natural n, k=1 is excluded; k=2..5 fail divisibility, while k=6 gives n=5. Thus p+n=6+5=11.
reviewer_notes: Assumes natural numbers are positive integers; with that convention k=6 is the smallest valid value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Suppose that the mean and median of the non-negative numbers 21, 8, 17, a, 51, 103, b, 13, 67, (a>b), are 40 and 21, respectively. If the mean deviation about the median is 26, then 2a is equal to:
questions.solution: Mean 40 gives a+b=80. The seven known values have total absolute deviation from median 21 equal to 183; total deviation is 9*26=234, so |a-21|+|b-21|=51. Since a>b and median is 21, a>=21>=b, so a-b=51. Solving with a+b=80 gives 2a=131.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let the line L1:x+3=0 intersect the lines L2:x−y=0 and L3:3x+y=0 at the points A and B, respectively. Let the bisector of the obtuse angle between the lines L2 and L3 intersect the line L1 at the point C. Then BC²:AC² is equal to:
questions.solution: A=(-3,-3), B=(-3,9), O=(0,0). OA·OB=-18, so angle AOB is obtuse. By the angle-bisector theorem AC/CB=OA/OB=sqrt(18)/sqrt(90)=1/sqrt(5); hence BC^2:AC^2=5:1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let the vertex \(A\) of a triangle \(ABC\) be \((1,2)\), and the mid-point of the side \(AB\) be \((5,-1)\). If the centroid of this triangle is \((3,4)\) and its circumcenter is \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(21(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.solution: Midpoint AB=(5,-1) gives B=(9,-4); centroid (3,4) gives C=(-1,14). Circumcenter (alpha,beta) satisfies 4alpha-3beta=23 and -alpha+6beta=48. Thus beta=215/21, alpha=282/21, and 21(alpha+beta)=497.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Suppose that two chords, drawn from the point \((1,2)\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2+x-3y=0\), are bisected by the \(y\)-axis. If the other ends of these chords are \(R\) and \(S\), and the midpoint of the line segment \(RS\) is \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(6(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.solution: If a chord midpoint on the y-axis is (0,k), its other endpoint is Q=(-1,2k-2). Substitution in the circle gives 4k^2-14k+10=0, so k=1 or 5/2 and the endpoints are S=(-1,0), R=(-1,3). Their midpoint is (-1,3/2), so 6(alpha+beta)=3.

questions.solution: Parametrize P=(2s,3s,3s-1), Q=(-t-1,t+2,4t). Since PQ is parallel to (1,-1,2), component relations give s=1/5 and t=-8/15. Then PQ=(-13/15,13/15,-26/15), so 225a^2=169(1+1+4)=1014.

questions.solution: A point on the line through (-2,-8,6) parallel to (1,-1,2) is Q=(k-2,-k-8,2k+6). Intersection with the first line gives k-3=(-k-9)/2=-2k-6, hence k=-1 and Q=(-3,-7,4). Therefore PQ^2=1+1+4=6.
